pathway.title: Cushman & Wakefield Ltd. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Recurring services income and low capital needs are the main support, but the recurrence is weaker than the label suggests: Services is 66% of 2025 revenue and largely recurring through multi-year contracts, and full-year free cash flow rose from USD 101.2 million in 2023 to USD 293.0 million in 2025, yet the company warns that many service agreements can be terminated for convenience on short notice or without notice, and 31.37% of revenue is reimbursed pass-through cost carrying substantially no margin. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, page 54; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C13; calculation C14

- Earnings are the weakest dimension because they swing with deal activity and costs do not follow: in 2023 fee revenue fell 9.89% and adjusted EBITDA fell 36.57%, so 45.86% of the lost fee revenue reached EBITDA, because direct employment cost absorbed only USD 373.9 million of the USD 716.7 million lost, other direct and overhead costs fell USD 82.8 million and indirect and overhead employment cost rose 6.34%; by 2025 fee revenue was still 2.58% below 2022 and adjusted EBITDA 26.99% below, with employment cost at 69.18% of fee revenue against 64.97% in 2022. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 74 and 92; 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 100–101; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

- Leverage has improved, but part of the improvement rests on add-backs and an upswing: net debt over adjusted EBITDA is 2.96x against 4.63x on unadjusted EBITDA, add-backs were 50.99% of reported EBITDA in 2025 and 22.75% in the nine months of 2026, and nine-month revenue rose 9.92% with adjusted EBITDA up 14.63%, led by Leasing up 20.32%, so creditors should treat the two leverage measures as a range. The effect of the October 21, 2026 redemption on net debt is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cwk.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation C6; calculation C13

- Liquidity and refinancing risk are low for the next three years: liquidity of USD 1,489.0 million is 1.78x the USD 835.9 million term loan due January 2030, the nearest maturity, the June 2026 amendment moved USD 1,200.0 million of term loan to 2033 at a lower margin, and the company says S&P and Moody's upgraded its ratings, which is management language; but 50.74% of the remaining principal falls due by 2031, so refinancing capacity depends on earnings holding up through 2028. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cwk_exhibit991-october212026re-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C10; calculation C13

- Cash generation is seasonal and was weaker in 2026 than earnings suggest, mainly because growth absorbed working capital: nine-month operating cash flow was USD 24.4 million against USD 83.1 million a year earlier, the company attributes the fall to USD 336.0 million of working capital used, USD 173.0 million more than a year earlier, and free cash flow converted 27.91% of adjusted EBITDA over the latest twelve months against 44.65% in 2025; the first quarter used USD 243.5 million of operating cash in 2026 against USD 162.0 million in 2025, and the fourth quarter of 2025 produced 75.59% of that year's operating cash flow, so year-end deleveraging depends on the fourth quarter. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cwk.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-Q_2026-03-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 81–82; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C12

- Financial policy is creditor-aligned on the evidence supplied but nothing supplied limits it: the company pays no dividend, prepaid USD 504.6 million of term loans since January 2024 and retired USD 650.0 million of 2028 notes, yet the credit agreement, the ranking of the debt and the shareholder register are not supplied, so the capacity of owners or management to change course is not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cwk.htm.jsonl, page 66; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C13; calculation C14

cells.text: Global commercial real estate services firm with about 53,000 employees in over 350 offices in nearly 60 countries, managing about 6.5 billion square feet; four service lines: Services, Leasing, Capital markets, Valuation and other
A people-based advisory and management platform: earnings follow staffing, client activity and deal volumes
Services 66%, Leasing 21%, Capital markets 8%, Valuation and other 5% of revenue; on service line fee revenue 51%, 30%, 12% and 7%
Contract Services anchors revenue, but Leasing and Capital markets make up a larger share of fee income

Contract income steadies cash flow; transaction fees move with deal volumes and credit market conditions
Gross contract reimbursables of USD 3,226.9 million, 31.37% of revenue, are reimbursed client costs with substantially no margin
Revenue overstates the earnings base; margins should be read on fee revenue
Americas 73%, EMEA 10% and APAC 17% of 2025 revenue; the United States was 69% of revenue and Australia 5%
Earnings are concentrated in the United States dollar economy and its commercial property cycle
Payment for property and equipment of USD 47.4 million, 0.46% of revenue; the company calls its operations not capital intensive
Low capital spending leaves most operating cash flow for debt service

Cash and net debt at interim dates are not year-end levels; the revolver and securitization bridge the cycle

runs.text: The first credit strength is a recurring contract base that needs little capital: Services is 66% of revenue under multi-year contracts, capital spending was USD 47.4 million or 0.46% of 2025 revenue, and full-year free cash flow rose from USD 101.2 million in 2023 to USD 293.0 million in 2025, so contract income funds fixed costs and interest while transaction fees add earnings, which lowers the chance that a deal slowdown alone exhausts cash. The second is falling leverage with long maturities: net debt over adjusted EBITDA fell from 4.35x at end-2023 to 2.96x, cash interest paid fell from USD 263.9 million in 2024 to USD 202.4 million over the latest twelve months, and no debt matures before January 2030, which lowers interest burden and refinancing pressure. The third is liquidity of USD 1,489.0 million at September 30, 2026, made of USD 489.0 million of cash and an undrawn USD 1,000.0 million revolver maturing October 2030, which is 1.78x the nearest maturity. The fourth is demonstrated market access: in June 2026 lenders agreed to reprice, extend to 2033 and increase the term loan by USD 352.5 million, and the company says its scale places it among the top three providers by revenue and workforce, which is management language. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, page 82; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C12; calculation C13

The first weakness is earnings that move with deal activity while overhead does not: the 2023 fall of 36.57% in adjusted EBITDA against a 6.06% fall in revenue shows operating leverage that raises leverage ratios quickly in a downturn, so creditors carry more cyclical risk than the recurring services share implies. The second is dependence on add-backs: unadjusted net leverage of 4.63x and unadjusted cash interest cover of 2.26x are the thinner measures, and add-backs were 50.99% of reported EBITDA in 2025, so the improvement in adjusted metrics is only as durable as the issuer's judgement that the items do not recur. The third is weak cash conversion in 2026, with nine-month operating cash flow of USD 24.4 million, which leaves the year dependent on a fourth-quarter inflow. The fourth is contract and talent fragility: service agreements can end on short notice and the industry has high turnover of revenue-producing advisors, so revenue and earnings can leave faster than the recurring label implies. The fifth is that legal protection and control are not established, which prevents a firmer view of financial policy and of structural priority. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, page 29; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2; calculation C9; calculation C13

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: No acquisition, sponsor transaction or new bond issue appears in the supplied documents for the period; the transactions are refinancings and repricings of existing secured debt. On June 12, 2026 the company amended its credit agreement to reprice USD 847.5 million of the term loan from 1-month Term SOFR plus 2.75% to plus 2.25%, extend that loan from January 2030 to June 2033 and add USD 352.5 million, giving a USD 1,200.0 million term loan whose proceeds were used to redeem part of the 2028 notes. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cwk.htm.jsonl, page 69; calculation C6

The 2028 secured notes, originally USD 650.0 million, were redeemed in three steps: USD 450.0 million in the second quarter of 2026, USD 50.0 million in August 2026 and the remaining USD 150.0 million on October 21, 2026, after which no long-term debt matures before 2030. Earlier, in 2025, the company repriced its 2030 term loans three times, prepaid USD 300.0 million of them, and cut and extended its revolver on October 21, 2025 to USD 1.0 billion maturing in October 2030. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cwk.htm.jsonl, page 44; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cwk_exhibit991-october212026re-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 111–112; calculation C5

The receivables securitization limit was raised by USD 50.0 million to USD 300.0 million on March 18, 2026 and its termination date extended to March 18, 2029; this is off-balance-sheet funding and not a new debt issue, and the effect of the refinancings on net debt is for the Financial foundation analysis. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cwk.htm.jsonl, page 38

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has improved but still depends on issuer add-backs: net debt was 2.96x issuer-adjusted EBITDA at September 30, 2026, down from 4.35x at end-2023, yet 4.63x on unadjusted EBITDA, so creditors need those add-backs to recur.

fields.value: Gross debt fell at every balance sheet date while adjusted EBITDA grew, so adjusted net leverage fell from 4.35x at end-2023 to 2.96x at September 30, 2026; on unadjusted EBITDA the improvement is smaller and uneven, with net leverage of 6.25x, 4.26x, 4.52x and 4.63x over the same four dates, because a non-cash USD 177.0 million impairment of an equity-method investment in 2025 and other add-backs sit between the two measures. Both sides of the ratio moved: net debt fell by USD 358.6 million between end-2023 and September 30, 2026 and adjusted EBITDA rose by USD 147.2 million from 2023 to the latest twelve months, with USD 300.0 million of debt prepayments in 2025 and net repayments of USD 151.7 million in the nine months of 2026 behind the debt side.

fields.value: - The filings print a dash, meaning nil, for several lines, which are stated as not supplied rather than zero: restructuring, impairment and related charges and impairment charges in the nine months of 2026; loss on debt extinguishment in 2024; impairment of equity method investment in 2023 and 2024; loss on disposition of business in 2025; acquisition of business in 2023, 2024 and the nine months of 2026; proceeds from disposition in 2023; proceeds from borrowings and debt issuance costs in 2024, 2025 and the nine months of 2025. This limits no ratio. Severity: Low. Action: none unless a later filing states an amount.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Lines of the annual cash flow statement that the nine-month statements do not present (impairment of equity method investment, loss on disposition of business and proceeds from disposition of business or other investments) are not supplied for the nine-month columns. This limits comparison of the nine months with the full year only. Severity: Low. Action: none.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The issuer states no unadjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA for every period is derived from net income, taxes, net interest and depreciation and amortization, and for the latest twelve months it is a built figure; it includes a USD 168.3 million equity-method loss in 2025. This limits unadjusted leverage and cover in every period. Severity: Medium. Action: read it beside the issuer-adjusted measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No discrete fourth quarter of 2025 and no 2025 quarter-end balance sheets are supplied, and the third quarter report prints only the prior year-end balance sheet, so trends between year-ends cannot be drawn from statements. This limits intra-year leverage trend. Severity: Medium. Action: derive the fourth quarter from the full year less nine months and label it derived.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No maturity ladder is printed at September 30, 2026, so the debt maturities table uses final maturity years and leaves the 0.25% quarterly term loan amortization in the final year; the ladder in the 2025 annual report predates the June 2026 refinancing. This limits near-term maturity conclusions. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the schedule of maturities from the next annual report.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The sources do not state how the term loans rank against the senior secured notes, so no facility is placed on the debt stack and ranking is not supplied for any instrument. This limits any priority conclusion. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the executed security and intercreditor documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The price of the October 21, 2026 redemption, any premium, accrued interest and the funding source are not stated, so the effect on net debt and pro forma leverage is not established. This limits the post-balance-sheet adjustment only. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the redemption notice.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No borrower-group, guarantor-group or restricted-group financial statements are supplied, only consolidated statements and a parent-only schedule that shows no debt at the parent. This limits structural analysis of which entity owes the debt. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain guarantor disclosures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The covenant is a springing net leverage test of 5.00x tested only when revolver borrowings exceed a threshold the filings do not state, defined in a credit agreement that is not supplied; headroom is therefore not calculable and none is inferred. Severity: High. Action: obtain the credit agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revolver letters of credit outstanding at September 30, 2026 are not stated in the third quarter report; the year-end 2025 figure is USD 6.6 million and the revolver capacity for letters of credit is the lesser of USD 220.0 million and undrawn capacity. This limits precision of undrawn availability only. Severity: Low. Action: use the stated undrawn revolver and label the letters of credit as not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The receivables securitization is off balance sheet, with USD 75.0 million of capital outstanding at September 30, 2026 against USD 120.0 million at year-end 2025, and is excluded from debt and from liquidity. This limits comparability with issuers that carry such funding as debt. Severity: Medium. Action: carry it as a named funding item beside debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Segment Adjusted EBITDA before 2026 and from 2026 sit on different corporate cost allocations, and the issuer no longer reports service line fee revenue or its Adjusted EBITDA margin, so segment margins cannot be traced across the change. This limits segment trend conclusions. Severity: Medium. Action: keep the two series apart.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Annual cash interest paid is taken from a supplemental note because the cash flow statement does not print it, and cash paid can differ from interest expense net of interest income (USD 216.6 million against USD 216.2 million in 2025). This limits cover precision slightly. Severity: Low. Action: none.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Instrument terms not stated in the sources read are marked not supplied: security and terms for finance lease liabilities and short-term borrowings, the revolver floor, and annual amortization as an amount. This limits the instrument register only. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the credit agreement.

fields.value: The strongest evidence against a creditor-aligned reading is what the supplied documents cannot show: no shareholder register, no board independence detail and no credit agreement, so nothing here proves that distributions, new secured debt or asset transfers are limited, and a sizeable holder could change policy through the board. Within the business, the Greystone exposure is the least bounded item, with 67 loans on the Fannie Mae loss-sharing list at September 30, 2026 and a company statement that additional loan losses could create a potentially material liability for the venture, and the change in reported measures from 2026 makes margin trends harder to verify. The view would weaken if a proxy statement showed a controlling holder with distribution ambitions, if executed debt documents showed wide restricted-payment capacity, if Greystone losses grew beyond the 40% interest the company describes, or if the consent decree obligations or state claims produced monetary outflows. It would strengthen if the documents confirmed broad ownership, independent directors and tight limits on distributions.

fields.value: Cushman & Wakefield's fundamental credit profile is adequate and improving: recurring services income, light capital needs and falling leverage support creditors, but earnings that swing with deal activity and reliance on issuer add-backs leave less cushion in a downturn than leverage ratios suggest.

When fee revenue fell 9.89% in 2023, adjusted EBITDA fell 36.57%; the same fall applied to the latest twelve months would put net leverage near 4.66x.

fields.value: - Earnings are the weakest dimension because they swing with deal activity and costs do not follow: in 2023 fee revenue fell 9.89% and adjusted EBITDA fell 36.57%, so 45.86% of the lost fee revenue reached EBITDA, because direct employment cost absorbed only USD 373.9 million of the USD 716.7 million lost, other direct and overhead costs fell USD 82.8 million and indirect and overhead employment cost rose 6.34%; by 2025 fee revenue was still 2.58% below 2022 and adjusted EBITDA 26.99% below, with employment cost at 69.18% of fee revenue against 64.97% in 2022.

The effect of the October 21, 2026 redemption on net debt is not established.

fields.value: - Financial policy is creditor-aligned on the evidence supplied but nothing supplied limits it: the company pays no dividend, prepaid USD 504.6 million of term loans since January 2024 and retired USD 650.0 million of 2028 notes, yet the credit agreement, the ranking of the debt and the shareholder register are not supplied, so the capacity of owners or management to change course is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against an adequate and improving profile is that the improvement is recent, cyclical and concentrated: Americas adjusted EBITDA margin on total revenue rose to 6.44% from 5.76% in the nine months, while EMEA revenue rose 15.16% and its adjusted EBITDA fell 7.25%, and Leasing and Capital markets are 29.38% of nine-month revenue against 27.49% a year earlier, so a reversal in deal activity would remove most of the gain; cash conversion has also weakened as earnings rose. The view would weaken if quarterly Leasing or Capital markets revenue turned negative, if the fourth quarter failed to restore operating cash flow, if the revolver were drawn at a quarter end, or if the unseen credit agreement or shareholder register showed room to distribute or add secured debt. It would strengthen if the next annual report showed fourth-quarter cash flow restoring free cash flow conversion, add-backs shrinking toward the 2026 nine-month share, and adjusted EBITDA holding in a weaker transaction quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Management outlook is the only forward evidence supplied, with no analyst, market or rating-agency forecast, so the outlook conclusion tests the company's targets against history and could move if an independent view were available.

fields.value: - Service line fee revenue is no longer reported from 2026, so margin resilience is measured on fee revenue only to 2025 and on total revenue and recast segment results for 2026, which weakens the claim that 2026 margins are higher on a like-for-like basis.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The covenant definition, security ranking and guarantor structure are not in the documents read, so the assessment that refinancing and liquidity risk are low assumes lenders keep the access shown in 2025 and 2026 and could change if the executed terms are tighter than the filings imply.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The share of cash flow that is seasonal is measured only for 2025, the one year with a derived fourth quarter, so the statement that the fourth quarter restores operating cash flow rests on a single year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first credit strength is a recurring contract base that needs little capital: Services is 66% of revenue under multi-year contracts, capital spending was USD 47.4 million or 0.46% of 2025 revenue, and full-year free cash flow rose from USD 101.2 million in 2023 to USD 293.0 million in 2025, so contract income funds fixed costs and interest while transaction fees add earnings, which lowers the chance that a deal slowdown alone exhausts cash. The second is falling leverage with long maturities: net debt over adjusted EBITDA fell from 4.35x at end-2023 to 2.96x, cash interest paid fell from USD 263.9 million in 2024 to USD 202.4 million over the latest twelve months, and no debt matures before January 2030, which lowers interest burden and refinancing pressure. The third is liquidity of USD 1,489.0 million at September 30, 2026, made of USD 489.0 million of cash and an undrawn USD 1,000.0 million revolver maturing October 2030, which is 1.78x the nearest maturity. The fourth is demonstrated market access: in June 2026 lenders agreed to reprice, extend to 2033 and increase the term loan by USD 352.5 million, and the company says its scale places it among the top three providers by revenue and workforce, which is management language.

fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, page 82; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 22–23; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C12; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is earnings that move with deal activity while overhead does not: the 2023 fall of 36.57% in adjusted EBITDA against a 6.06% fall in revenue shows operating leverage that raises leverage ratios quickly in a downturn, so creditors carry more cyclical risk than the recurring services share implies. The second is dependence on add-backs: unadjusted net leverage of 4.63x and unadjusted cash interest cover of 2.26x are the thinner measures, and add-backs were 50.99% of reported EBITDA in 2025, so the improvement in adjusted metrics is only as durable as the issuer's judgement that the items do not recur. The third is weak cash conversion in 2026, with nine-month operating cash flow of USD 24.4 million, which leaves the year dependent on a fourth-quarter inflow. The fourth is contract and talent fragility: service agreements can end on short notice and the industry has high turnover of revenue-producing advisors, so revenue and earnings can leave faster than the recurring label implies. The fifth is that legal protection and control are not established, which prevents a firmer view of financial policy and of structural priority.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cushman & Wakefield is a global commercial real estate services firm with revenue of USD 10,288.2 million in 2025, about 53,000 employees in nearly 60 countries and four service lines; the United States is 69% of revenue. Contract Services income is described by the company as mostly recurring and is the predictable base against which fixed costs and interest are met, Leasing earns fees after leases are signed with some visibility from renewal dates, Capital markets fees arrive at deal close, and the reimbursed cost of contract work passes through revenue at substantially no margin, so revenue overstates the earning base and the creditor-relevant earnings pool is fee revenue of USD 7,061.3 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 4–6; 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, page 54; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The group parent is a Bermuda holding company listed in New York that has no debt of its own, with the debt guaranteed jointly by substantially all material operating subsidiaries in the United States and certain in the United Kingdom, each pledging substantially all of its assets; no sponsor or controlling shareholder is described, so creditor alignment rests on stated policy of no dividends and debt repayment and not on knowing who controls decisions. The joint ventures, the 40% Greystone venture and the 35% Onewo venture, sit outside consolidated EBITDA, with Greystone carrying loss-sharing obligations under its lender agreement with Fannie Mae.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is partly recurring and partly cyclical, and the cyclical part is growing faster: nine-month revenue rose 9.92%, with Services up 7.13%, Valuation and other up 5.99%, Capital markets up 10.23% and Leasing up 20.32%, which lifted Leasing and Capital markets to 29.38% of revenue from 27.49%. Services contracts have multi-year terms and high switching costs, but many can be terminated for convenience on short notice, and no client concentration figure is printed beyond the statement that the client portfolio is highly diversified. The creditor consequence is that the contract floor under revenue is real but not contractually locked, so a fall in transaction income is only partly cushioned.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cwk.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 27 and 29; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2023 episode shows the cyclical half: revenue fell 6.06% from USD 10,105.7 million in 2022 to USD 9,493.7 million in 2023, and fee revenue fell 9.89%; the documents read do not state why, and the 2025 annual report describes clients delaying transaction decisions when credit is scarce or costly as a recurring risk, so the fall is evidence of sensitivity and not of one cause.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins can be defended only in part under volume pressure. Direct employment cost fell 9.22% in 2023 against a 9.89% fall in fee revenue, consistent with the commission-based pay the company describes for many United States leasing and capital markets professionals, and absorbed USD 373.9 million of the USD 716.7 million of lost fee revenue; but indirect and overhead employment cost rose USD 41.6 million, other direct and overhead costs fell only USD 82.8 million together, other segment items that support adjusted EBITDA fell USD 27.1 million, and the adjusted EBITDA margin on fee revenue fell from 12.40% to 8.73%. Employment cost has since risen to 69.18% of fee revenue from 67.01%, so a decline of the same size would now take a larger share of lost fees.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2024-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, page 92; 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 100–101; calculation C1; calculation C2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Recovery since 2023 has lifted the adjusted margin on fee revenue to 9.29% but not rebuilt it to the 12.40% of 2022: from 2023 to 2025 fee revenue rose 8.11%, employment cost rose 11.60% and adjusted EBITDA rose 15.10%, an incremental margin of 16.25% against the 45.86% decremental margin on the way down, so the asymmetry favours the downside. The nine-month margin on total revenue improved to 5.90% from 5.66%, entirely in the Americas.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 100–101; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 3 and 14; calculation C3; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital spending is small, USD 47.4 million or 0.46% of 2025 revenue and USD 81.5 million or 0.74% of latest twelve month revenue, but it rose to USD 58.5 million in the nine months of 2026 from USD 24.4 million, 2.40 times, a USD 34.1 million increase that the company attributes primarily to relocating its New York office, so the rise is more likely one-off than a new run rate, though that is an analyst reading. Capex flexibility is therefore a minor lever, and the cash drains that matter are working capital and outflows to other non-current assets, which include receivables from advisors and other employees of USD 492.8 million at September 30, 2026: the outflow was USD 24.7 million in 2023, USD 58.0 million in 2024 and USD 121.2 million in 2025, and USD 72.0 million in the nine months of 2026. The company attributes the fall in nine-month operating cash flow to USD 336.0 million of working capital used, USD 173.0 million more than a year earlier, with higher contract assets of about USD 38.0 million, higher prepaid expenses of about USD 24.0 million and lower accounts payable of about USD 98.0 million, so part of the weakness is growth-related and timing-related and part of it may reverse.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 66 and 68; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cwk.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 81–82; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow turns only part of adjusted EBITDA into cash, 17.75% in 2023, 28.70% in 2024, 44.65% in 2025 and 27.91% over the latest twelve months, after cash interest of USD 202.4 million and cash taxes of USD 59.3 million in 2025 against a tax provision of USD 26.0 million. Nine-month free cash flow was negative USD 34.1 million, and the fourth quarter of 2025 supplied 75.59% of full-year operating cash flow, so debt service is met from a back-loaded year; the company states a free cash flow conversion target of 60% to 80% of adjusted net income, which is a different base from the one used here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, page 122; IR_Third-Quarter-2026_presentation.pdf, page 6; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is high but the group has scale: competitors include several large global peers and many smaller local firms, in-house corporate real estate departments and outsourcing companies, and the company says it is among the top three providers by revenue and workforce, which is management language, so scale helps win multinational mandates but does not remove competition for renewals. New entrants matter more in regional brokerage, where firms are smaller and licensing requirements are one barrier, than in integrated facilities management, where global scale is needed, so the earnings most exposed to entry are the commission lines that also swing with the cycle. Substitutes are in-house teams and technology: the company is investing in artificial intelligence and says AI-driven demand for data centres supports leasing, but it does not quantify any fee erosion from technology. Buyers hold power through short-notice termination rights and the possible growth of large corporate clients, and suppliers matter mainly through third-party contractors whose costs are passed through, and through advisor compensation, where high turnover makes talent the real supplier.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 10 and 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22; 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 27 and 29

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Macroeconomic and regulatory factors are a material credit driver because demand for transactions depends on interest rates, credit availability, tariffs and employment, as the company states, and because hybrid working has changed the use of commercial property. Revenue outside the Americas was 27% of 2025 revenue, but the company invoices in the currency of its costs, so currency translation is a secondary risk; the Bermuda corporate income tax under the global minimum tax initiative adds tax uncertainty without a quantified effect.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths: contract Services income that funds fixed costs; scale across occupier and investor clients; low capital spending; falling leverage and a maturity wall that starts in 2030. Weaknesses: adjusted EBITDA that falls faster than fee revenue; add-backs that separate adjusted from unadjusted leverage; seasonal and back-loaded cash flow; unestablished covenant, ranking and ownership terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities that could improve credit quality: data centre and industrial leasing demand and a stronger Capital markets cycle that lift fee income; continued repayment from fourth-quarter cash flow; term loan margin reductions as ratings improve. Threats that could weaken it: a repeat of the 2023 transaction slump, tariffs and credit tightening that delay deals, loss-sharing losses at Greystone, and tax or litigation outcomes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main credit supports are scale, contract income, small capital needs, falling leverage and long maturities; the constraints are cyclical earnings, add-back dependence, seasonal cash flow and missing legal terms; the trend is improving on adjusted measures and mixed on unadjusted cash conversion. Liquidity is adequate at September 30, 2026, refinancing capacity is adequate while earnings hold and rating improvements continue, and financial policy is supportive on conduct but unproven on legal limits. The missing datapoints that would give a firmer opinion are the executed credit agreement, the shareholder register, the 2026 fourth quarter cash flow and the numeric 2028 targets the company refers to.

fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX99.1_2026-09-30_cwk_exhibit991-october212026re-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the company guides to revenue growth at the mid-to-high end of 6% to 8%, adjusted EPS growth of 18% to 23% and free cash flow conversion of 60% to 80% of adjusted net income for 2026, and the latest twelve month conversion is 60%; these are management targets, and nine-month revenue growth of 9.92% in reported dollars is above the top of the revenue range, though the company states its growth rates in local currency so the comparison is indicative only. Tailwinds are improved macro conditions, leasing demand in office, industrial and data centres, and a fourth quarter that is the strongest of the year. Headwinds are tariffs, rates and credit conditions that delay transactions, and EMEA and APAC margin pressure, with EMEA adjusted EBITDA down while revenue grew.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: IR_Third-Quarter-2026_presentation.pdf, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 14 and 44; calculation C6; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the main change is the interest cost reset: swaps fixing USD 1,500.0 million of the USD 2,035.9 million of term loans run off from August 2027, with USD 400.0 million expiring in 2027, USD 550.0 million in 2028 and USD 550.0 million in 2029, leaving USD 535.9 million unhedged today and more after each expiry, so interest sensitivity rises before the 2030 maturity; the company's numeric 2028 targets are not supplied. Each 100 bp of rate move on the unhedged amount costs about USD 5.36 million a year, small against USD 202.4 million of cash interest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 19 and 23; EX99.1_2026-09-30_cwk_exhibit991-october212026re-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside is a transaction slump that repeats the 2023 pattern. Credit conditions tighten, clients delay leases and sales, Leasing and Capital markets fees fall, and employment cost does not fall as fast: replaying the 36.57% fall in adjusted EBITDA on the latest twelve months of USD 717.3 million removes USD 262.3 million to leave USD 455.0 million, which would put net debt over adjusted EBITDA near 4.66x with net debt unchanged at USD 2,120.3 million and cash interest cover near 2.25x, and would turn free cash flow of USD 200.2 million to about negative USD 62.1 million before cost action. The effect of the October 21, 2026 redemption on net debt is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, page 92; 10-K_2025-12-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, page 101; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C2; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first break would come in the fourth quarter, which carries 36.38% of annual adjusted EBITDA and 75.59% of operating cash flow, followed by a first-quarter cash trough, when operating cash flow was negative USD 243.5 million in 2026 against negative USD 162.0 million in 2025 and cash was USD 600.6 million at March 31, met from year-end cash, the USD 1,000.0 million revolver and receivables funding; a revolver draw would bring the springing net leverage test into play, whose definition is not supplied. Management levers are commission-linked pay, capital spending of 0.74% of revenue, and no dividend. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity event over two years because no debt matures before 2030, but a downturn lasting to 2028 would meet the 2030 term loan of USD 835.9 million with weaker earnings and leverage near the replayed level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cwk.htm.jsonl, page 66; 10-Q_2026-03-31_cwk.htm.jsonl, pages 2 and 5; 10-Q_2026-06-30_cwk.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C5; calculation C8; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Cushman & Wakefield presents an adequate business profile supported by contract services income, scale, light capital needs and falling leverage, but credit quality is constrained by earnings that follow deal activity, reliance on issuer add-backs and seasonal cash flow. Cash-flow durability appears adequate on a full-year basis and weaker on the nine-month evidence, because free cash flow converted 27.91% of adjusted EBITDA over the latest twelve months. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on holding earnings through 2028, before the 2030 term loan, and on the unseen covenant and ranking terms. The primary downside path is a transaction slump that cuts fee income faster than costs, which would lift leverage to near 4.66x on a replay of 2023. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement, the shareholder register, fourth-quarter 2026 cash flow and numeric company targets. Top risk: earnings that swing with deal activity.
